characters.name: Kari Woodsmock (the king’s daughter)
characters.description: A gentle princess driven from her home by her cruel stepmother, she endures hardship, keeps three strange tokens, and hides in a wooden smock while fate leads her to a prince.
characters.look: A slender young woman of about eighteen with a fine-boned face, high cheekbones, a slim nose, wide-set hazel eyes under straight dark-copper brows, a dimple in her chin, her face and hands black with soot and her long, wavy copper hair in a messy braid dulled with ash. Over a plain grey linen shift she wears the wooden smock: a stiff, bell-shaped garment of thin, grey-brown wooden boards laced together like the staves of a barrel, reaching from her neck to her ankles, and wooden clogs.

characters.name: Kari in the Copper Dress
characters.description: Kari on the first Sunday, riding to church in a dress that shines like the copper wood.
characters.look: A slender young woman of about eighteen with a fine-boned face, high cheekbones, a slim nose, wide-set hazel eyes under straight dark-copper brows, a dimple in her chin, fair skin and long, wavy copper hair falling loose down her back under a thin copper band. She wears a long, flowing gown of shining copper cloth that glows warm orange-pink like polished copper, embroidered with small copper leaves, with long copper-coloured gloves and soft copper slippers.

characters.name: Kari in the Silver Dress
characters.description: Kari on the second Sunday, in a dress stitched all over with silver, on a horse with a silver-embroidered saddlecloth.
characters.look: A slender young woman of about eighteen with a fine-boned face, high cheekbones, a slim nose, wide-set hazel eyes under straight dark-copper brows, a dimple in her chin, fair skin and long, wavy copper hair in one loose braid woven with silver ribbons. She wears a long gown stitched all over with silver thread that glitters like frost, trimmed with rows of tiny silver leaves, a short silver-grey riding cape and silver slippers, and carries a slim riding whip with a silver handle.

characters.name: Kari in the Gold Dress
characters.description: Kari on the third Sunday, in a dress of almost nothing but gold and diamonds, with little shoes of gold.
characters.look: A slender young woman of about eighteen with a fine-boned face, high cheekbones, a slim nose, wide-set hazel eyes under straight dark-copper brows, a dimple in her chin, fair skin and long, wavy copper hair flowing loose under a slender gold band. She wears a long, full gown of gold cloth sewn all over with small sparkling diamonds that glitter like dew, and two small, pointed shoes of shining gold.

characters.name: The Blue Bull
characters.description: A powerful enchanted bull who feeds and protects Kari, fights three trolls, and leaves behind a hidden source of magic that continues to aid her.
characters.look: A huge, powerful bull, taller at the shoulder than a grown man, with a glossy, deep cornflower-blue coat that always looks freshly polished, a paler blue-grey muzzle, big, soft dark-brown eyes with long lashes, two long, smooth cream-white horns curving forwards and up, large soft ears, a curly tuft of darker blue hair between the horns, a long tail ending in a navy-blue tassel, and dark grey hooves. Calm, wise and kind.

characters.name: The Stepmother Queen
characters.description: A jealous, calculating queen who starves and beats her stepdaughter and schemes to have the blue bull killed to destroy Kari’s secret help.
characters.look: A tall, thin queen of about forty with a long, pinched face, a sharp pointed nose, narrow pale-green eyes, thin arched eyebrows, a small mouth turned down at the corners and jet-black hair scraped into a tight bun under a tall, spiky silver crown. She wears a stiff, high-collared gown of dark slate-grey wool with a narrow white linen collar, a black velvet cloak and many heavy rings, and holds a white linen handkerchief.

characters.name: The Queen's Daughter
characters.description: The Queen's daughter, as ugly and mean as the King's daughter is kind and fair, who gets the gold shoe on and is dressed as a bride.
characters.look: A gangly young woman of about eighteen with a long, sour face, a pinched, turned-up nose, small squinting pale-green eyes, a pouting mouth and thin, straw-pale hair in two stiff braids that stick out sideways. She wears an over-trimmed dress of sour gooseberry-green wool covered in far too many pink ribbons, white stockings and pointed green shoes on very long, big feet.

characters.name: The Prince
characters.description: The castle’s young prince who scorns the clattering kitchen girl yet falls hopelessly in love with the mysterious church-going lady and searches for her through the lost gold shoe.
characters.look: A broad-shouldered prince of about twenty-two with a proud, stubborn face, a strong jaw, a slightly hooked nose, bright blue eyes under straight fair brows and thick, wavy honey-blond hair swept back from his forehead and falling to his collar, under a small gold crown. He wears a heather-purple wool tunic with gold trim over a cream linen shirt, a short dark-green cloak fastened with a round gold brooch, black hose and soft black leather boots.

characters.name: The Man in the Cliff
characters.description: A man who comes out of the cliff whenever Kari knocks with the stick, and gives her dresses of copper, silver and gold and a horse to ride to church.
characters.look: A small, sturdy old man no taller than a young girl, with a round, rosy, wrinkled face, a big round nose, twinkling bright-blue eyes under bushy white eyebrows and a long, silky white beard that reaches his knees. He wears a long, hooded moss-green cloak with a wooden toggle, a brown tunic with a rope belt and soft brown boots, and carries a small brass lantern that glows warm yellow.

characters.name: The Three-Headed Troll
characters.description: The troll who owns the copper wood, and who comes rushing out with all three heads when the King's daughter tears off a leaf.
characters.look: A squat, pot-bellied troll about twice as tall as a man, with pale, chalky grey-white skin like weathered limestone, speckled with grey freckles and patches of moss, short bandy legs and long dangling arms. It has three bald, egg-shaped heads on three thick necks, each with a big red bulbous nose, small round orange eyes, one crooked tooth and tufts of stiff orange hair behind the ears. It wears a ragged brown sacking kilt, with a curved cow horn of ointment hanging from its rope belt.

characters.name: The Six-Headed Troll
characters.description: The troll who owns the silver wood, twice as strong as the first, who fights the bull for three whole days.
characters.look: A tall, lanky troll about three times as tall as a man, with knobbly, rusty-orange skin like iron-stained rock, patched with grey lichen, long skinny arms and legs and huge flat feet. On a wide, bony pair of shoulders sit six small heads in a row, each with a long droopy nose, sleepy yellow eyes, big flappy ears and wispy white hair like bog cotton. It wears a moth-eaten grey wool tunic, with a curved cow horn of ointment on a string at its belt.

characters.name: The Nine-Headed Troll
characters.description: The terrible guardian of the golden wood, whose many heads keep reviving one another until the blue bull finally defeats him in a brutal week-long struggle.
characters.look: An enormous, pear-shaped troll as tall as six men, with lumpy skin the dusky pink and purple of blooming heather, a huge round belly and short, stumpy arms and legs like tree stumps. Along its broad shoulders sit nine small round heads in a row, each with puffy cheeks, a tiny snub nose, small black eyes under bushy grey brows, big round ears and a shock of spiky grey hair. It wears a huge patched brown hide tunic, with a curved cow horn of ointment hanging from its belt.

places.name: the Church Hill
places.look: A small, dark, tarred stave church with steep, tiered shingle roofs, carved dragon heads on the gables and a tall arched door inside a low, covered wooden porch, standing on top of a green hill below the castle. A low stone wall surrounds the churchyard, a few birches with yellowing leaves stand around it, and a gravel path with a few stone steps leads up to the porch past a wooden hitching rail for horses.
